title: At 11 years old, she just broke a chess record that stood for over two decades.

sources.text: ChessBase - Bodhana Sivanandan, youngest ever WGM at 11
Gulf News - Indian-British chess prodigy Bodhana Sivanandan makes history at 11

caption:
At 11 years old, she just broke a chess record that stood for over two decades.

Playing top board for England at the 46th Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, she secured her third and final WGM norm - breaking a record held jointly by Kateryna Lagno and future Women's World Champion Hou Yifan, both of whom earned the title at age 12.

Born in India, based in Harrow, UK, she took up chess as a hobby during the COVID-19 pandemic. In July 2025, at age 10, she had already become the youngest player ever to earn a WGM norm - breaking a record previously held by Hou Yifan.

A Viksit Bharat by 2047 is built partly on stories like this - proof that talent with Indian roots keeps setting the pace globally, in fields nobody would have predicted a generation ago.
